name: Brushed Metal
desc: A machined metal panel under a shop lamp that will not hold still — the anisotropic highlight smears perpendicular to the brush grain and travels as the lamp orbits, wandering satin grain on a slightly oil-canned face, breaking into a rotating dark cross on a sunburst disc or a field of planished facets under the hammer.

energy.doc: how hard the highlight burns — dull satin through to a blazing specular streak

scale.doc: coarseness of the whole surface — grain wander, brush tooth, waviness and hammer facets together

polish.doc: 0 = coarse brush, a wide soft glow · 1 = fine polish, a razor-thin travelling streak

density.doc: brush tooth, how straight the grain runs, and the hammer strike count

hue.doc: re-tints the alloy (210 = cool steel; ~35 reads brass/bronze)

speed.doc: how fast the lamp orbits the panel

y.doc: lamp height — low rakes hard and long, high sits flat and broad

style.doc: brushed: straight satin grain, the highlight a long band smearing across it · sunburst: circular brushing — a dark anisotropic cross sweeps round as the lamp orbits · hammered: planished, a lattice of dished hammer facets each catching the lamp · anodised: heat-tinted titanium, the interference colour locked to the topography rather than the lamp · blueprint: non-representational — the reflectance field alone as hard iso-bands on a machinist chart, no material

act.doc: rake: the lamp orbits steadily · buff: the polish comes up and falls away across sections, dull to mirror · turn: the lamp holds still and the part rotates on the table instead

seed.doc: re-brushes the panel — new grain wander, waviness and hammer pattern
